BiblicalUsage: mastízō is to scourge, and it occurs once, in Acts 22:25. There, as they bind Paul with thongs to scourge him, he asks the centurion whether it is lawful to scourge a man who is a Roman and uncondemned. The word is the whip stopped by a question.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mastízō shows me that Paul knew his rights and used them, and that a Roman scourging was no small thing to face.
